Dissolution of joint ownership and convenient divisibility With regard to judicial division, the right of each co-owner to obtain their share in kind pursuant to Article 718 of the Italian Civil Code prevails over the request for allocation of the entire share of the majority shareholder if the asset is conveniently divisible.
 “Convenient divisibility” pursuant to Article 720 of the Italian Civil Code exists if the division does not involve excessively costly technical problems, does not affect the intended use of the property and does not depreciate its overall value. In this specific case, the presence of double entrances and the possibility of creating independent units confirms the divisibility in kind.
Exclusive enjoyment of the common property and civil fruits The mere exclusive enjoyment of immovable property by a co-owner does not, in itself, give rise to compensable damage or an obligation to pay compensation to the other co-owners. Pursuant to Article 1102 of the Italian Civil Code, exclusive use is legitimate if it does not alter the intended use of the property and does not prevent the other co-owners from making similar use of it. The right to compensation arises only if the non-user co-owner can demonstrate that they expressed a desire to enjoy the property directly and that this right was denied to them. 
Reimbursement of sums for the purchase of property exclusively owned by the other spouse A spouse who purchases a property with their own money, even if it is registered exclusively in the name of the other spouse, is entitled to reimbursement of the sums paid pursuant to Articles 192 and 2033 of the Italian Civil Code.
 This claim for restitution works in the same way as the provisions for legal community property when personal money is used for an asset belonging to the other spouse. It is the beneficiary's responsibility to prove that the payment was made for a different reason, such as a gift or the fulfilment of family contribution obligations, in order to avoid the obligation to make restitution.
